caption: Make clever use of a limited set of road tiles.
content: Early on, you don't have many tiles, so you can't connect roads the way you'd like. You need to get creative — take detours or change your starting point.
From here on, we'll assume our available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_road.2t.ul}.

content.caption: Take detours
content: Let's think how to reach the road below in this Area.
If we connect the roads via the shortest route, it would look like this, but since we don't have @t{forest_road.2t.dl}, this placement isn't possible.
By taking a detour like this and using the pre-placed road tile @t{forest_road.2t.dl}, we can connect the road.
Note that you don't necessarily have to pass through the pre-placed road tiles. For example, in this Area, you can connect the road while avoiding the bottom-right @t{forest_road.2t.ul}.

content.caption: Change the starting point
content: Let's think how to reach the road below in this Area.
To connect the road from left to bottom, we need @t{forest_road.2t.dl}, but we don't have it.
So first, connect the road from left to right, and reach the right.
Then we can connect from right to bottom and reach the road below.
